messages:
Sam (sales): FYI — Aurelia Health wants a perf POC next week. Their ask: sustained 200 qps, 99p < 350ms, multi-region failover, and an estimate of per-request cost. Can we run?
Alicia (sales): tagging eng/SE for scope. they care about PHI compliance too (SOC2 + KMS). timeline: 3 days to validate baseline, then 2 days of stress.
Maria (SE): Got it. Need to confirm model + prompt mix. Do they use a chat-style system or single-turn completions? Approx tokens/customer request?
Sam (sales): It's single-turn summarization of clinical notes. Avg input 1.2k tokens, output ~120 tokens. Mostly deterministic; small sampling.
Lina (eng): For 200 qps steady-state with that token size we need to plan batching and KV-cache. Do they require streaming? Also: target SLO 99p <350ms — tight given token count. Is 99p measured for first token or full response finish?
Sam (sales): They measure end-to-end (full response).
Owen (sre): Multi-region means warm replicas and health-routing. We'll need to test cold-start tails. Plan should include cold-start probe and warm steady-state. Also KMS/HSM adds extra latency for key unwrap during init; need to quantify.
Maria (SE): Proposed perf plan (short):
- Step 1 (smoke, 1h): baseline single-region, 10 qps, confirm correctness.
- Step 2 (ramp, 3h): linear ramp to 200 qps across 2 AZs, measure p50/p95/p99 and failure rate.
- Step 3 (soak, 6h): sustain 200 qps, check memory/KV cache hit rate and tail.
- Step 4 (spike/cutover test): simulate region failover, 5min 500 qps spike to observe throttling/fallback.
- Artifacts: stdout logs, per-request traces, token counts, prom metrics export.
Maria (SE): Example runner command we'll use (redwood local perf runner):
```
# warmup + 1 minute sample
perf-runner --target https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \\n  --concurrency 10 --ramp 3m --duration 1m \\n  --payload-file sample_payload.json --auth-token $REDWOOD_KEY
```
Maria (SE): sample_payload.json snippet:
```json
{ "model": "open-redwood-7b", "input": "<clinical notes...>", "max_tokens": 150 }
```
Lina (eng): For accuracy of results ensure we run with and without prefix/KV cache enabled. Caching will massively change 99p. Also test quantized medium model variant for cost tradeoff.
Sam (sales): Pricing question from Aurelia: what delta does quantized model + cache give vs baseline? They want a rough ballpark to include in renewal forecast.
Lina (eng): Ballpark: baseline hosted gen (un-cached) ~ $0.045 per 1k output tokens for this model scale. With aggressive KV prefix cache and 8-bit quant variant we'd estimate unit cost reduction ~45-60% for steady-state. For 200 qps * 120 out tokens avg -> ~864M tokens/day un-cached; with cache hits could drop to ~300M tokens/day effective. Exact depends on hit rate.
Owen (sre): Note: if they require KMS HSM signing per-request, add ~12-18ms to per-request latency (measured on similar PoC). That could push 99p over target on cold misses. Consider using session-level keys or caching key unwrap.
DeployBot: loadtest-started: thread=5367891234 run_id=run-2026-06-10-01 region=us-west-2
Maria (SE): Quick early results after ramp to 200 qps (first 12m sample): p50=90ms, p95=160ms, p99=380ms, error rate=0.2%. Observed 99p misses correlate with KV cache miss and occasional GPU queueing spikes.
Lina (eng): 99p 380ms — slightly above target. Two mitigations to try: 1) enable prefix caching (should drop 99p by ~80ms) 2) drop to quantized model-medium for tail-sensitive endpoints. Also increase reserved capacity to avoid GPU queueing at tail.
Maria (SE): Ran the same run with prefix cache enabled: p50=88ms, p95=140ms, p99=295ms, error rate=0.1% — meets 99p <350ms. Cache hit rate reported 71% for this workload.
Sam (sales): Great — can we capture cost delta for both runs so Aurelia can pick?
Maria (SE): Yes. Quick numbers from run:
- No-cache, standard model: est tokens/day ~864M -> est cost/day ~$38,880 (hosted unit rates).
- Cache + quantized variant: effective tokens/day ~300M -> est cost/day ~$15,000. (These are estimates; we will provide formal quote.)
Owen (sre): Also add risk note: multi-region failover test produced a 30–45s window of higher latency while replicas ramped cold; recommend warm standby and traffic cutover policy.
Alicia (sales): Can SE/eng produce a two-page summary for Aurelia + an appendix with the exact test commands/metrics and a recommended config for Dedicated vs Hosted? They want both technical and procurement folks to sign off.
Maria (SE): I'll draft the summary and attach raw CSVs. Lina — can you add a short note on reserved capacity sizing (how many GPUs, burst buffer) and expected SLA for 200 qps?
Lina (eng): Yep. Suggest 4 reserved GPUs in us-west-2 with burst pool of 1-2 extra for spikes; this keeps tail below 350ms with prefix caching and quantized fallback. I'll add numbers.
Sam (sales): Security Q: Aurelia asked whether the Private deployment option supports their HSM requirements and audit logs. Any blockers?
Owen (sre): Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; audit logs exist but we need to confirm retention policy. No blocker, but enterprise procurement may request SOC2 + customer audit docs — SE should include pointer to compliance pack.
Maria (SE): I'll include compliance pack link and add the exact steps to enable session key caching to avoid per-request HSM latency.
Sam (sales): Cool. Who owns next steps and timeline?
Alicia (sales): Owners: Maria — summary & artifacts (deliver EOD tomorrow). Lina — reserved capacity sizing + cost appendix (EOD tomorrow). Owen — security notes + KMS latency mitigation doc (72h). I'll schedule a 30m recap with Aurelia for Wednesday.
Maria (SE): ack :thumbsup:
Lina (eng): ack
Owen (sre): ack
Sam (sales): thanks team — will update Aurelia and send calendar invite.
